venue.name: Sidney Museum and Archives
venue.description: The Sidney Museum and Archives is a local history museum in the lower level of the Olde Post Office building on Beacon Avenue in Sidney. It was set up in 1971 and its permanent collection holds more than 8,000 artifacts, many of them on show in the permanent galleries. A featured exhibit changes through the year, and a LEGO brick train table is on permanent display in the front area. The museum is not running guided school programs at the moment, but classes are welcome to come through on their own.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: For elevator access, enter through the rear of the building off Fourth Street, near the Dental Hygiene Office and REUZ Room. Inside the elevator, press B to reach the main level of the Museum.

venue.hours_notes: Open 7 days a week from 10:00am to 4:00pm. Closed December 25th, December 26th, and January 1st.
venue.seasonal_notes: The annual LEGO brick exhibit returns in December 2026 and runs until around March 2027. A LEGO brick train table with a train on a circular track is on permanent display year round.

programs.name: Self-guided class visit
programs.description: The school programs page currently says to check back for more information soon, so there is no guided program running. Classes are welcome to visit on a self-guided basis. Arrange it by emailing outreach@sidneymuseum.ca or calling 250-655-6355. The site does not publish a price, a group size limit, an age range or a visit length.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the permanent galleries at their own pace, looking at objects from the history of Sidney, North Saanich and the Saanich Peninsula, plus whatever featured exhibit is up. In the front area there is a LEGO brick train table with a village and a train running on a circular track.
programs.our_note: The museum is downstairs in the Olde Post Office building, so plan the route in before you arrive. The front door is down two short flights of stairs and the step-free way in is round the back off Fourth Street, where a volunteer has to open the lower doors for you. Nothing about cost, group size or how long to allow is published, so one phone call will settle the whole visit.
programs.practical_summary: Both levels are reachable by elevator if you come in from the rear on Fourth Street. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and how many adults you need are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so ask when you arrange the date.
programs.evidence: If you are interested in brining your class to the Sidney Museum on a self-guided visit please email

images.alt: A two storey red brick building with white trim and a gabled roof, with a round Sidney Museum sign hanging from a post over the sidewalk and a railed staircase leading down at street level.
